scope: R-006 candidate A device trials: early stop point with no display MMIO and no wait

tests.purpose: positive control: prove EnumaStageCheckpoint(10) actually fires

checkpoint_execution_control.conclusion: the extra 5 s of MicroSecondDelay appears almost fully in the return time, so EnumaStageCheckpoint(10) executed and ResetCold() did reset the SoC
checkpoint_execution_control.residual: the 0.73 s shortfall against the nominal 5 s is within Android boot-time spread and is not treated as a separate effect

statistical_limit: with an assumed 15% per-run stall rate, five clean trials have a 44% chance of showing no stall at all, so this batch does not exclude the early exit from being stall-prone; it only bounds a high per-run rate. Reaching ~90% exclusion of a 15% rate needs about fifteen clean trials (0.85^15 = 8.7%).
r006_reading: all five returned, so the branch 'reset exit is stable when no display MMIO has been touched' is favoured, and the timeout is pushed to the later dispatch/display path. This is a directional conclusion, not a quantified one.
main_hypothesis: the two timeouts and the historical S-001/250849f/S-002/S-003 cases all sit after SimpleFbDxe starts touching 0x0ae00000..0x0ae84207; a powered-down MDP domain can hang the AHB path on first access, which would look exactly like a permanent dark screen with no USB enumeration and would be independent of how many registers the probe reads
